mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 3 Series 316i engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 3 Series 316i engine replacement typically costs between £700 and £5,000 depending on the engine code and condition type. A used N43B16A for the E90 316i starts from around £400, while a fully rebuilt unit with warranty ranges from £2,000-£3,200. The N13 turbo engine for the F30 316i is more expensive - rebuilt units from £3,000-£5,000. Specialist fitting adds £520-£910 in labour.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a BMW 3 Series 316i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common early warning sign is a rattling noise from the engine on cold start - often described as a 'rattle' that lasts 1-2 seconds before quietening down. As the chain stretches further, you may notice engine misfires, rough idling, a check engine light, or rattling that persists when the engine is warm. If ignored, the chain can snap, causing catastrophic engine damage.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 3 Series 316i?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the value of your car and the extent of the damage. For an E90 316i worth £2,500-£6,000, a rebuilt engine at £2,000-£3,200 is a significant investment - often exceeding the vehicle's value at the lower end. For an F30 316i worth £5,000-£12,000, a rebuilt engine at £3,000-£5,000 may be worthwhile if the rest of the car is in good condition. For older E46 models worth under £3,000, replacement is rarely cost-effective.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the BMW 316i and 318i engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 316i and 318i often share the same engine block but with different displacements or tuning. In the E90 generation, the 316i uses the 1.6-litre N43B16A (122hp), while the 318i uses the 2.0-litre N43B20A (143hp). In the E46 generation, the 316i used the 1.6-litre N46B16 or 1.8-litre N42B18, while the 318i used the 2.0-litre N42B20. Always verify compatibility with your specific VIN.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 3 Series 316i engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 3 Series 316i engine replacement typically takes 2-3 days for a specialist workshop to complete, assuming the replacement engine is already in stock with the supplier. The labour time for the E90 316i (N43) is approximately 8-10 hours, while the F30 316i (N13) is slightly longer at 10-12 hours. Supply-only delivery usually takes 1-3 working days depending on your location.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between reconditioned, rebuilt and used BMW 316i engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: Used engines are taken directly from donor vehicles - they're the cheapest option but come with unknown mileage and history. Reconditioned engines are professionally cleaned, tested, and have worn components replaced - they offer a good balance of cost and reliability. Rebuilt engines are fully stripped, cleaned, machined, and reassembled with new parts including pistons, rings, bearings and gaskets - they're the most expensive but come with a 12-month warranty and are the closest you'll get to a new engine.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 3 Series 316i - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 316i has served as the entry-level petrol 3 Series since the E30 generation of the late 1980s, evolving from a 1.6-litre carburettor-fed unit to a 1.6-litre turbocharged four-cylinder. Across its history, the 316i badge has been applied to petrol engines spanning six chassis generations.

milestones.description: 1991 (E30) - M40B16, 1.6-litre petrol, 102hp - fuel-injected SOHC four-cylinder, replaced the carburettor-fed 316
1998 (E36) - M43B16, 1.6-litre petrol, 102hp - updated SOHC four-cylinder with Bosch Motronic
2001 (E46) - M43B16, 1.6-litre petrol, 102hp - carried over into early E46 production
2005 (E46) - N42B18 / N46B16, 1.8-litre / 1.6-litre petrol, 115hp - Valvetronic, double VANOS
2011 (E90) - N43B16A, 1.6-litre petrol, 122hp - direct injection, naturally aspirated
2016 (F30) - N13B16A, 1.6-litre turbocharged petrol, 136hp - TwinPower Turbo, 8-speed automatic

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the BMW 3 Series 316i is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: BMW 3 Series 316i Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW 316i has worn many different petrol engines over six generations, from the robust M43 to the high-strung N43 and the turbocharged N13. The most common replacement-intent searches today come from owners of the E90 316i with the N43 petrol engine, followed by the F30 316i with the N13 turbo. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: N43 Timing Chain Guide Failure - Why the BMW 3 Series 316i N43 Fails
problems.rootCause: The N43's timing chain guides are made of plastic that becomes brittle over time. When they break, fragments drop into the sump and block the oil pump intake, causing oil starvation and potential engine seizure. The original tensioner was too short and allowed the chain to become slack. The chain itself rarely breaks - it's the guide debris that kills the engine.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: New chain, guides, tensioner - oil pan drop and debris removal
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if caught before engine seizure
When engine has seized or guides have caused catastrophic damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2007-2011 E90 316i is worth approximately £2,500-£6,000 `[THIRD-PARTY]`. At the lower end, replacement cost often exceeds vehicle value - evaluate scrap value before committing. At the higher end, a rebuilt engine may be viable if the car is in excellent condition otherwise.
problems.recommendation: The N43 is a high-maintenance engine. If you're experiencing misfires, loss of power, or rattling from the timing chain area, have a specialist inspect it immediately. If the engine has seized, compare the cost of a rebuilt unit against the vehicle's market value - in many cases, it may be more economical to sell the car for parts and buy another.

problems.h4: N13 Timing Chain Failure - Why the BMW 3 Series 316i N13 Turbo Fails
problems.rootCause: The N13 uses the same substandard timing chain components as the N20 and N47 engines. The chain can stretch, slip, or snap, all of which can result in complete engine failure. Oil dilution (fuel getting into the oil) is also a known issue on this engine.

repairOptions.longevity: When chain has snapped or engine is damaged

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2012-2016 F30 316i is worth approximately £5,000-£12,000 `[THIRD-PARTY]`. At the lower end, a rebuilt engine may represent 40-60% of the vehicle's value - a significant investment but potentially worthwhile if the car is otherwise in good condition. At the higher end, a rebuilt unit with warranty is a sound investment.
problems.recommendation: If you hear a rattling noise from the engine on cold start, get the timing chain inspected immediately. A £1,200-£1,800 specialist chain replacement is far cheaper than a £3,000-£5,000 engine replacement. If the chain has already snapped, a rebuilt engine through a specialist is typically better value than a main dealer replacement.
